morningSummary: The day's major developments include an Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, the arrival of US envoys in Moscow for Ukraine negotiations, Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka formally submitting his resignation, and renewed international debate over security in the Taiwan Strait. France faces a weaker economic outlook after Moody's reduced its 2026 growth forecast to 0.2%. In Africa, Ebola remains a serious concern in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, while Kenya has begun a 42-day countdown following the discharge of its last known patient. COP31 negotiations in Türkiye have exposed deep divisions over climate finance, fossil fuels and the pace of the global energy transition.
breaking: GAZA — An Israeli airstrike hits the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis. Gaza Civil Defence reports six deaths, including a surgeon, and around 20 injuries. Israel says it targeted Hamas operatives at the complex.

UKRAINE — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow following US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi. A prisoner exchange was agreed in principle, but no ceasefire or peace settlement has been reached.
INDONESIA — Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka formally submits his resignation to the country's parliamentary assembly amid controversy surrounding his eligibility and educational qualifications.
FRANCE — Moody's lowers its forecast for French economic growth in 2026 to 0.2%, citing political uncertainty, fiscal pressures and higher borrowing costs.
G7 — Foreign ministers warn that China's increasingly assertive activity east of Taiwan threatens regional stability, freedom of navigation and international shipping.
AFRICA — The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to report major Ebola transmission, with more than 11,000 confirmed cases and over 5,000 related deaths in the latest available figures.

KENYA — The last known Ebola patient has been discharged. A 42-day countdown has begun, with 23 December identified as the earliest possible date for declaring the outbreak over if no new cases emerge.
UNITED STATES — A three-storey building collapses in Brooklyn, killing at least two people and injuring at least 17, according to initial city reports. The cause remains under investigation.
EUROPE — France says the EU is expected to approve further sanctions against Russia on Monday, including additional entities and banks.
PERU — Pope Leo receives large crowds during his visit to Peru, describing the country as his homeland and calling for renewed public trust and social responsibility.
COP31 — Climate negotiations in Antalya expose disagreements over fossil fuels, emissions reductions and financial support for developing countries.
NIGERIA — The ADC leadership and presidential nomination dispute remains before the courts following the party's appeal against the Federal High Court ruling.

featured.title: US Envoys Meet Putin as Ukraine Peace Negotiations Enter Another Critical Stage
featured.summary: Washington's diplomatic effort continues in Moscow after negotiations in Abu Dhabi produced progress on a possible prisoner exchange but no agreement on territory or a ceasefire.
featured.content:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow on Thursday for discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The meeting follows two days of US-mediated negotiations between Russian and Ukrainian representatives in Abu Dhabi.

The Abu Dhabi discussions produced an agreement in principle to arrange another major prisoner exchange. However, the parties remain divided over the future of occupied Ukrainian territory, post-war security guarantees and the role European countries should play in negotiations.

Ukraine has rejected Russia's demand that it surrender the whole of the Donbas region as part of a settlement. Moscow, meanwhile, has expressed reservations about European participation and the possibility of European troops being deployed in Ukraine after a ceasefire.

The American envoys are also expected to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin. More than 40 European leaders and guests are gathering in Ireland to discuss Ukraine and wider European security.

WHY IT MATTERS: A prisoner exchange would be a significant humanitarian development, but it must not be confused with a ceasefire or a peace agreement. The central questions of sovereignty, territory and Ukraine's future security remain unresolved.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Attention will focus on the outcome of the Moscow meeting, the planned discussions with Zelenskyy and whether the parties can agree on a wider negotiating framework involving European partners.

topStories.title: Israeli Strike on Nasser Hospital Kills Six, Including Surgeon
topStories.summary: An airstrike hits the surgery department of Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis. Gaza Civil Defence reports six deaths and around 20 injuries.
topStories.content:
An Israeli airstrike struck the surgery department at Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday. Gaza Civil Defence reported that at least six people were killed, including surgeon Rezik Abushira, while around 20 others were wounded.

The strike damaged part of the hospital's surgical facilities. Medical services were disrupted as staff dealt with casualties and damage to the complex.

The Israeli military said the operation targeted Hamas personnel allegedly operating from the hospital complex. Those allegations should be distinguished from independently verified facts about the damage and casualties.

Hospitals and medical personnel receive special protection under international humanitarian law. That protection can be affected if a medical facility is used for acts harmful to the enemy, subject to strict legal conditions and safeguards.

WHY IT MATTERS: Damage to a functioning hospital affects patients who may already have limited access to surgery, emergency treatment and specialist care.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Independent verification, protection of remaining medical services and investigation of the circumstances surrounding the strike remain important.

topStories.title: Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Formally Submits Resignation
topStories.summary: Gibran Rakabuming Raka submits his resignation to the parliamentary assembly amid controversy over his eligibility for office.
topStories.content:
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka formally submitted his resignation to the People's Consultative Assembly on Thursday. The development follows intense political pressure and controversy over court decisions concerning the educational qualifications used to support his 2024 vice-presidential candidacy.

Gibran's resignation creates a significant political challenge for President Prabowo Subianto and the governing coalition. The parliamentary assembly must now follow the constitutional procedure for processing the vacancy and selecting a replacement.

The political dispute also reflects tensions involving former President Joko Widodo, Gibran's father, and the political alliance that helped bring Prabowo and Gibran to power.

WHY IT MATTERS: A vice-presidential resignation of this kind raises questions about political stability, constitutional accountability and the relationship between electoral rules and public confidence.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The parliamentary process, the president's role in nominating replacement candidates and the political response from the parties will determine the next stage.
topStories.source: Reuters; The Jakarta Post; CNA; ANTARA

topStories.title: Moody's Cuts France's 2026 Growth Forecast to Just 0.2%
topStories.summary: The ratings agency now expects only modest economic growth, below the French government's 0.5% target.
topStories.content:
Moody's has reduced its forecast for French economic growth in 2026 to 0.2%, a substantial downgrade from its earlier projection. The new estimate is below the French government's 0.5% target and the Bank of France's forecast of around 0.3%.

The agency points to political uncertainty, higher bond yields, fiscal constraints and tighter credit conditions as factors weighing on the economy. France is also facing difficult budget negotiations and pressure to control public debt.

The downgrade does not mean that France is officially in recession. It is a warning that economic activity is weaker than previously expected and that the country's fiscal and political challenges may continue to restrict growth.

WHY IT MATTERS: Slower growth can affect employment, household purchasing power, business investment and government revenue. It may also make it harder for the government to reduce its deficit.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Investors and businesses will watch budget negotiations, borrowing costs, employment data and the next economic forecasts.
topStories.source: Moody's; AFP; MoneyVox; The Local France

topStories.title: G7 Warns China's Activity Near Taiwan Threatens Regional Stability
topStories.summary: Foreign ministers meeting in Paris raise concerns over maritime security and the possibility of unilateral changes to the Taiwan Strait status quo.
topStories.content:
Foreign ministers from the Group of Seven countries issued a joint declaration following their meeting in Paris on 9 and 10 November. The statement expressed serious concern about China's increasingly assertive activities in waters east of Taiwan.

The G7 said these developments threaten regional stability, freedom of navigation and the safety of international shipping. It opposed attempts to change the status quo through force or coercion and called for peaceful dialogue across the Taiwan Strait.

Taiwan welcomed the declaration, describing peace and stability in the region as essential to international security and prosperity. Beijing has consistently rejected what it views as foreign interference in its internal affairs.

WHY IT MATTERS: The Taiwan Strait is strategically important for international trade, maritime routes and the global technology supply chain. Any escalation could have consequences far beyond East Asia.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Diplomatic reactions, military activity and efforts to maintain communication between regional powers will remain under close observation.
topStories.source: G7 Joint Declaration; France Diplomatie; Taiwan Presidential Office

topStories.title: DR Congo Ebola Outbreak Remains Severe as Kenya Begins Recovery Countdown
topStories.summary: The DRC continues to report extensive transmission, while Kenya has discharged its final known patient and begun a 42-day countdown.
topStories.content:
The Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to face a major outbreak of Bundibugyo virus disease. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control reported 11,042 confirmed cases and 5,387 related deaths in the DRC in figures available through 9 November.

The regional situation requires continued surveillance, laboratory capacity, contact tracing and protection for health workers. Nigeria has also reported one case in October, with the patient medically evacuated to Switzerland and 62 contacts identified in the available ECDC update.

Kenya has reached an important milestone after its last known Ebola patient was discharged on 11 November. The World Health Organization says the country began a 42-day countdown on 12 November. If no new cases are detected, Kenya could be declared free of the outbreak on 23 December.

WHY IT MATTERS: The outbreak demonstrates the importance of cross-border surveillance, early diagnosis, public communication and properly equipped health services.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The DRC's response remains urgent. Kenya must maintain monitoring and rapid response arrangements throughout the countdown; it has not yet been declared Ebola-free.
topStories.source: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control; WHO Africa; Kenya Ministry of Health

topStories.title: Deadly Building Collapse in Brooklyn Leaves Residents Dead and Injured
topStories.summary: A three-storey building collapses in Flatbush, New York. Emergency crews continue rescue and recovery operations as officials investigate the cause.
topStories.content:
A three-storey building collapsed in the Flatbush neighbourhood of Brooklyn, New York, on Wednesday afternoon. Initial reports from city authorities said at least two people had died and at least 17 had been injured, including children and a firefighter.

More than 250 emergency responders were reported to have attended the scene. Firefighters and rescue teams used specialist equipment to search the rubble and assess whether anyone remained trapped.

The building collapsed into an adjacent construction area. Officials have said that the cause remains under investigation. The proximity of the construction site is relevant to the inquiry, but it does not establish that construction activity caused the collapse.

WHY IT MATTERS: The incident raises urgent questions about building safety, construction oversight, emergency preparedness and the protection of residents in densely populated urban areas.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Investigators will examine the building's condition, construction records and the circumstances surrounding the collapse. Casualty figures may change as official information is updated.
topStories.source: The Associated Press; Washington Post; RTÉ; ABC7 New York

topStories.title: France Says EU Plans New Russia Sanctions Targeting Banks and Entities
topStories.summary: French Europe Minister Benjamin Haddad says the EU is expected to approve further sanctions on Monday.
topStories.content:
France's Minister Delegate for European Affairs, Benjamin Haddad, said on Thursday that the European Union is expected to approve another package of sanctions against Russia on Monday.

Haddad said the proposed measures would target 150 additional entities and 50 banks, with France having proposed a substantial part of the list. The announcement describes an expected decision, not sanctions that have already entered into force.

The measures form part of the EU's wider effort to maintain economic pressure on Russia over its war against Ukraine. The sanctions process requires agreement among member states and formal adoption before the measures become operational.

WHY IT MATTERS: Financial restrictions can affect Russia's access to international banking, trade networks and entities involved in supporting its war effort. They can also have implications for European businesses and financial compliance.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: EU member states are expected to consider the package on Monday. The final scope and implementation details will depend on the formal decision.

topStories.title: Pope Leo Draws Huge Crowds During Emotional Return to Peru
topStories.summary: The Pope's visit to Peru attracts large crowds as he calls for public trust, social responsibility and attention to the country's challenges.
topStories.content:
Pope Leo's return to Peru has drawn large crowds in Lima, where thousands of people gathered to see him during his visit. The Pope has described Peru as his homeland, reflecting the years he spent in the country as a missionary and bishop before becoming pontiff.

During the visit, he called on political leaders to address the country's troubled past and rebuild public trust. He also spoke about rising crime and the responsibility of institutions to protect vulnerable people.

The visit carries particular significance because of the Pope's personal history in Peru. His programme includes public events and visits to locations connected with his earlier ministry.

WHY IT MATTERS: The visit combines religious significance with wider questions about public trust, social cohesion and the role of faith leaders in national life.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The Pope is expected to continue his programme in Peru, including visits to communities connected with his earlier service.

topStories.title: COP31 Negotiations Expose Deep Divisions Over Climate Finance and Fossil Fuels
topStories.summary: Countries at the Antalya summit disagree over emissions reductions, energy transition priorities and the financial responsibilities of richer nations.
topStories.content:
The COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, has moved into difficult negotiations as governments attempt to reconcile competing priorities. Small island states are demanding faster emissions reductions, while developing countries are pressing wealthier nations to provide more financial support for clean energy, climate adaptation and recovery from climate-related damage.

European leaders have backed proposals to expand electrification. Fossil-fuel-producing countries, including Venezuela, have defended continued use of oil, gas and coal as part of their development strategies.

A separate financing development was announced as the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank agreed to provide Türkiye with a climate policy financing package worth $1.6 billion. The package is intended to support reforms, climate resilience and investment in renewable energy.

WHY IT MATTERS: Climate negotiations are not only about emissions targets. They also involve the cost of adaptation, energy security, development priorities and the question of who should pay for the transition.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Negotiators must turn competing national positions into an agreed outcome. Announced financing commitments should not be confused with money already disbursed.
topStories.source: Reuters; Associated Press; Canada Government; Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank

topStories.title: ADC Leadership Dispute: Appeal and Stay Application Remain Key to Atiku's 2027 Prospects
topStories.summary: The party has challenged the Federal High Court judgment affecting the David Mark-led leadership and its presidential nomination. The application for a stay must not be confused with an order already granted.
topStories.content:
The African Democratic Congress is continuing its legal challenge following the Federal High Court judgment of 5 November 2026 concerning the David Mark-led party leadership and decisions taken under that leadership, including the presidential nomination associated with former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar.

The party announced that it had filed an appeal and an application seeking a stay of execution. It also notified the Independent National Electoral Commission of the legal steps and urged the commission to exercise restraint while the dispute proceeds.

The distinction between an appeal and a stay is important. Filing an appeal does not automatically suspend the judgment. The stay application must be considered and granted by a competent court before it can have that effect.

INEC's position has also been linked to obtaining and examining the certified true copy of the judgment. The commission must act on the legal documents and any subsequent court orders rather than political claims or assumptions.

WHY IT MATTERS: The dispute has implications for opposition organisation, candidate nominations and the legal preparations for Nigeria's 2027 general election.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: The Court of Appeal proceedings, any ruling on the stay application and INEC's formal response will be central to determining the next stage. No final outcome of the appeal should be assumed.
topStories.source: Premium Times; Channels Television; TheCable; INEC statements

leaders.headline: Washington continues diplomatic engagement over Ukraine
leaders.report: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have travelled to Moscow for discussions with Vladimir Putin following US-mediated negotiations in Abu Dhabi.
leaders.background: The talks have produced progress on a proposed prisoner exchange but no settlement on territory or post-war security.
leaders.implications: The US administration faces pressure to demonstrate that its diplomatic initiative can produce practical progress without compromising Ukraine's sovereignty.
leaders.radiantWavesView: The outcome should be assessed through verifiable agreements, humanitarian results and the positions of all parties.

leaders.name: Emmanuel Macron
leaders.headline: France faces economic pressure and a prominent role in G7 diplomacy
leaders.report: France is leading the G7 presidency and has been active in diplomatic discussions on Ukraine and Indo-Pacific security. Moody's has also reduced its 2026 growth forecast for France to 0.2%.
leaders.background: France is dealing with budget pressures, political uncertainty and weak economic growth while seeking to maintain influence in European and international affairs.
leaders.implications: The government must balance international commitments with domestic economic and fiscal challenges.
leaders.radiantWavesView: International leadership is most sustainable when accompanied by credible economic management and public accountability.

leaders.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
leaders.headline: Nigeria's political environment remains focused on the 2027 election cycle
leaders.report: The ADC leadership and nomination dispute continues to shape the opposition landscape as legal proceedings develop.
leaders.background: Nigeria's political parties are preparing for the next general election amid public debate over economic conditions, governance and political accountability.
leaders.implications: The handling of political disputes and the credibility of electoral institutions will be important to public confidence.
leaders.radiantWavesView: RadiantWaves will assess government and opposition claims against evidence, legal decisions and measurable policy outcomes.

leaders.name: Atiku Abubakar
leaders.headline: Atiku's political future remains tied to the ADC legal dispute
leaders.report: The Federal High Court judgment affecting the ADC leadership and nomination is under challenge through the party's appeal process.
leaders.background: The ADC has said it filed an appeal and a stay application. The application for a stay must be determined separately; filing it does not automatically suspend the judgment.
leaders.implications: The legal outcome could affect opposition preparations and candidate nominations for 2027.
leaders.radiantWavesView: The next decisive developments will be judicial decisions and INEC's response to certified court documents.

leaders.name: Mark Carney
leaders.headline: Canada remains engaged in European security discussions
leaders.report: Canada's leadership is participating in international discussions on European security and climate policy.
leaders.background: Canada is a G7 member and has continued to engage with partners on Ukraine, international trade and climate finance.
leaders.implications: The country's diplomatic choices affect transatlantic relations and cooperation among G7 partners.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Canada's role should be judged by the practical commitments it makes on security, trade and climate cooperation.

leaders.name: Vladimir Putin
leaders.headline: Putin receives US envoys amid renewed Ukraine diplomacy
leaders.report: The Russian president is meeting US envoys after Abu Dhabi negotiations produced an agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange.
leaders.background: The parties remain divided over occupied territory, security guarantees and Europe's role in any settlement.
leaders.implications: Moscow's response will influence whether the diplomatic process can move beyond limited humanitarian agreements.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Any agreement must be assessed against its terms, implementation and respect for Ukraine's sovereignty.

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.headline: China faces renewed G7 criticism over Taiwan Strait activity
leaders.report: The G7 declaration has raised concern about Chinese activity east of Taiwan and called for peaceful resolution of cross-strait issues.
leaders.background: China rejects foreign involvement in what it considers its internal affairs, while Taiwan and several international partners emphasise regional stability and freedom of navigation.
leaders.implications: The issue remains central to Indo-Pacific security and global trade.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Diplomatic engagement and restraint remain essential to reducing the risk of escalation.

leaders.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
leaders.headline: Ukraine maintains its position on territory and security guarantees
leaders.report: Ukraine has rejected Russian demands over the Donbas and is seeking meaningful security guarantees as diplomatic discussions continue.
leaders.background: US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi produced a proposed prisoner exchange but no breakthrough on the central issues.
leaders.implications: The terms of any settlement will have consequences for Ukraine's sovereignty and wider European security.
leaders.radiantWavesView: A durable peace requires credible security arrangements and the meaningful participation of Ukraine.

leaders.name: Ursula von der Leyen
leaders.headline: EU weighs further sanctions against Russia
leaders.report: France says a new sanctions package targeting additional entities and banks is expected to be considered on Monday.
leaders.background: The EU continues to coordinate economic measures with partners while supporting Ukraine.
leaders.implications: The effectiveness of sanctions depends on implementation, enforcement and cooperation among member states.
leaders.radiantWavesView: The final measures and their enforcement should be monitored rather than treating a proposed package as already adopted.

leaders.name: Andy Burnham
leaders.headline: UK political debate intersects with climate and energy policy
leaders.report: The COP31 debate includes proposals to expand electrification and strengthen energy security, with UK political voices participating in the discussion.
leaders.background: Energy affordability, investment and climate targets remain central questions in British political debate.
leaders.implications: The challenge is to reconcile household costs, industrial competitiveness and emissions commitments.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Policy proposals should be assessed by their affordability, implementation timetable and measurable impact.

leaders.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leaders.headline: African cooperation remains important as regional health risks persist
leaders.report: The Ebola outbreak in Central Africa underlines the importance of cross-border public-health coordination and regional preparedness.
leaders.background: African governments and public-health agencies continue to face pressure to strengthen disease surveillance and emergency response.
leaders.implications: Regional coordination can reduce the risk of cross-border transmission and protect health systems.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Public-health preparedness requires sustained investment, transparent reporting and cooperation across borders.

leaders.name: Marine Le Pen
leaders.headline: French opposition politics remains active ahead of the 2027 presidential contest
leaders.report: France's political parties and potential candidates are positioning themselves ahead of the next presidential election.
leaders.background: Economic pressures, public services, immigration and national identity remain important issues in the French political debate.
leaders.implications: The political field may influence the direction of French domestic and European policy.
leaders.radiantWavesView: RadiantWaves will distinguish confirmed candidacies, legal developments and campaign claims from political speculation.

todaysBigQuestion.question: Can international diplomacy deliver lasting peace and security when the central disagreements over sovereignty, territory and political trust remain unresolved?
todaysBigQuestion.context: Ukraine negotiations, the G7's concerns over Taiwan and the humanitarian consequences of conflict in Gaza demonstrate the limits and importance of diplomacy.
todaysBigQuestion.invitation: What should be the first priority for international leaders: ceasefires, security guarantees, humanitarian protection or long-term political agreements?

radiantWavesPerspective.title: Beyond Headlines: Accountability Must Follow Every Major Decision
radiantWavesPerspective.content:
Today's developments underline the importance of evidence, transparency and accountability. A proposed prisoner exchange is not a peace agreement. A pending appeal is not a court order suspending a judgment. A forecast is not a confirmed economic outcome. An announced climate-finance package is not necessarily money already delivered.

RadiantWaves Media will continue to distinguish verified facts from allegations, political statements and projections. Our responsibility is to provide readers with context, explain why developments matter and identify what evidence or decisions should be watched next.

sourcePolicy.title: RadiantWaves Editorial and Verification Policy
principles: Verify major claims against reliable reporting or primary documents.
Distinguish allegations from independently established facts.
Do not describe an appeal as automatically suspending a court judgment.
Do not describe proposed sanctions as adopted measures.
Do not present forecasts as confirmed economic outcomes.
Do not use unrelated photographs to illustrate news stories.
Identify illustrative or generated images clearly when they are used.
Provide source attribution and context while maintaining original reporting and analysis.
